text:
alex: Heads up — p99s jumped right after the v2.4 rollout on ded-qa-3 around 12:08UTC. p95 ~220ms -> ~820ms, p99 ~1.2s -> ~2.9s. Not a normal transient.

maria: saw the alert, pulling traces now. any tenant obvious from the initial spike?

alex: tenant-78 had a burst but this looks broader. profiler shows kernel selection flip on lots of batches (cutlass -> custom_fp16) and KV cache hit rate dropped. also subtoken density increased after tokenizer tweak in v2.4.

tim: can you paste the profiler top lines and KV stats? curious if it’s memory pressure vs kernel heuristics.

alex: quick summary from perf window (120s): attention_cuda time +2.4x, kv_cache_lookup +3.3x, token_split ops +4.7x. KV hit rate down ~12%, eviction rate up. seq-len tail moved right: median ~320 -> ~340, 95th 820 -> 1200 due to more subtokens.

infra-bot: perf-profiler report: window=120s cluster=ded-qa-3 model=v2.4
- top ops: attention_cuda 42% (delta +2.4x), kv_cache_lookup 18% (+3.3x), token_split 9% (+4.7x)
- kv_evictions=9.8%

alex: command we ran to collect samples:
```
perf-trace --cluster ded-qa-3 --window 120s --filter model=v2.4 > /tmp/prof_v2.4.txt
```

jess: v2.4 included the tokenizer microchange that collapses some unicode sequences differently. that increased subtokenization for emoji/unicode sequences in certain inputs — explains seq-tail shift.

maria: interesting — that could increase KV cache working set and also change batching (more long sequences -> fewer samples per batch) which interacts with kernel-selection heuristics.

tim: I pushed a routing patch to prefer v2.3 tokenizer for requests with predicted seq_len > 1024 (simple heuristic) so we can canary rollback just the tokenization change. applying 10% canary now.

sre-oncall: canary applied at 12:18UTC (10% traffic to v2.3-tokenizer). early signals: canary p99 ~1.1s, remainder still 2.7s.

alex: good. immediate mitigations: 1) canary rollback of tokenizer (done), 2) temporary kernel-selection guard to avoid switching to custom_fp16 for batches with avg_subtokens > 2.2, 3) bump KV cache capacity on noisy hosts while we investigate.

jess: will create console dashboard cards for per-tenant KV eviction rate and a short-window alert: kv_eviction_rate > 8% in 1m -> pager.

maria: I'll run an offline sim with the v2.4 tokenizer on our seq-dist generator and try reproducing kernel flip; also run the quantized kernels to ensure we can reproduce the slow path.

tim: note for postmortem: add subtoken-density check to tokenizer CI + fuzzing of unicode/emoji to prevent regressions that shift seq distribution.

alex: created ticket INF-3492 linking profiler dump and flamegraph: https://perf.internal/redwood/flame/v2.4-1960001234 and /tmp/prof_v2.4.txt. Assigning to runtime+ml infra.

jess: will own dashboard+alert (INF-3493). Also proposing a batching heuristic change to prefer max_batch_size when seq_len variance low, and small-batch path for high-tail traffic.

maria: local sim reproduced kernel-selection flip when avg_subtokens > 2.1. kernel selector is choosing custom_fp16 because of lower theoretical FLOP cost but runtime memory access pattern makes it slower for long kv rows.

alex: thanks — follow-ups: (a) revert tokenizer change in v2.4 for full rollout, (b) add kernel-selection guard and test harness, (c) surface per-tenant kv eviction in console, (d) postmortem with action items.

infra-bot: DeployBot: routing change for v2.4-tokenizer -> v2.3-tokenizer (canary 10%) applied successfully at 12:18UTC.
